newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says 'real' trade deficit less than $1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Manila says 'real' trade deficit less than $1 bln.

text.p: The Philippine government said on Wednesday the country's widening trade deficit would not appear so high if foreign investment figures and earnings from Filipinos working overseas were included in the data.

Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista said that if portfolio and foreign direct investments were included, "the 'real' gap in our trade/investments is less than $1.0 billion which is not a major worry".
"Many countries have already reported trade in terms of goods and services -- such as the United States, Britain, Singapore, Australia, Japan, Australia, etc," he added.
The Central Bank recently said the country's merchandise trade deficit was expected to reach about $12.0 billion this year from $9.091 billion in 1995.
In the first eight months of this year, the trade deficit was $8.147 billion compared with $5.559 billion a year earlier.
